Stats

SCL_Oliver
Oliver is in the House in Deep Shadows, within the Shadow-Cursed Lands region in Act Two.

Overview

Appearance

Oliver appears to be a small olive-skinned tiefling child with grotesque shadowed gashes infecting his right eye and torso.

If the interacting party member passes an  Arcana check to sense his true nature, the aesthetics of the Shadow Curse are wiped from his body. Subsequently, he resembles more of a typical tiefling child, with his heterochromia still intact. Certain classes gain bonuses to this check, while Monks can choose an alternative  Insight check.

Involvement

Act two

Oliver is in the House in Deep Shadows. If a party member approaches, he asks them to 'play with' him. If humored, Oliver says he wants to play hide-and-seek, and turns himself invisible to go "hide."

When a party member first enters the ruined house a  Perception check is made, failing it lets the conversation start. They can study the boy if they do not already know he is Thaniel:

  • [ARCANA] Study the boy. Try to understand his true nature. (DC 14)
  • [DRUID] [WISDOM] A familiar magic exudes from the boy. Try to commune with it. (DC 14 )
  • [MONK] [INSIGHT] The child's ki feels... uneven. At odds. Why? (DC 14)

Oliver insists on playing hide and seek, and if refused, summons  Daddy,  Mummy, and  Doggy, who initiate combat.

Playing with Oliver

While "playing" with Oliver, walking up to his invisible model usually causes him to become "found." Automatic perception checks may be rolled, but for unknown reasons, these checks (on failure) do not always seem to disqualify the party from "finding" Oliver.

"Round One"

After "finding" Oliver for the first time, he immediately starts a conversation with the party member who found him. He is upset but can be invited to play again, which he happily accepts but with additional rules to the game, while adding you are better than the others, presumably referencing the Githyanki corpses littered around the house.

"Round Two"

Oliver vanishes while starting the "second round" of his game, triggering turn-based mode for all nearby characters, and three hostile shadow-like entities appear;  'Daddy',  'Mummy', and  'Doggy'. Among other tactics, it is possible to use a  Potion of Invisibility and run to the house.

If the party is able to sneak past his 'family' and speak with him again, he gives the  Ring of Shadows as a prize, even though he suspects the party cheated. If his family spots party members but they are defeated in combat, Oliver claims he won and awards the party with a 'second prize' – the same ring. If the party manages to pickpocket the Ring of Shadows from Oliver during the second round of hide and seek, a mundane silver band (worth 18 gold) is given instead as a reward.

His 'family' then disappears.

Playing both games of hide and seek with Oliver grants the following inspirations:

  • ⁠Child at Heart ( Urchin background)
  • ⁠Child's Play ( Outlander background)

Lifting the Shadow Curse

Advancing through the quest ⁠Lift the Shadow Curse with  Halsin ultimately requires that the party return to Oliver and convince him to reunite with  Thaniel.

Regardless of whether Oliver's game was played, the party can confront him with their new information about Thaniel and his identity. Oliver becomes upset, summons a portal, and disappears through it. The party can interact with this portal to travel to his new location, upon which combat begins. Oliver's new location is near the center of Reithwin Town at X: -152 Y: -26.

Once his protective dome is destroyed, Oliver complains about being disturbed and says he does not want to go back to Thaniel, who he perceives as having abandoned him. The party can choose to be kind when convincing Oliver to rejoin Thaniel and be whole again, or be aggressive; they can also let Halsin handle it.

Oliver always agrees to rejoin with Thaniel, but being aggressive about it causes Halsin to lose approval, while allowing him to handle it or being kind gives a large boost to his approval. Talking with Thaniel in camp reveals the Shadow Curse may only be lifted after  Ketheric Thorm is defeated once and for all.

Combat

Allies

  •  Daddy
  •  Mummy
  •  Nightdome
  •  Shadow Plush - may be summoned as often as every other round after the first
  •  Shadow Friend - 5x (5 additional Shadow Friends are summoned each round by Oliver)

Encounter Details

After running away Oliver moves to a protective magic bubble called the  Nightdome, which reflects double damage back at the attacking party member.

During this fight, Oliver does not leave his bubble. However, once per round he uses  Friends Until The End. This ability summons five  Shadow Friends. After the first round, use of this ability can summon a  Shadow Plush into the fight. If these shadow entities are not killed every round, it results in a growing number of them on the battlefield.

The Nightdome must be destroyed to resolve this combat encounter. Defeating Oliver's summoned Shadow allies reduces the health of the Nightdome without it retaliating against the party. Defeating Daddy, Mummy, or Shadow Plush deals 60⁠⁠Force to the dome, while defeating the Shadow Friends deals 10⁠⁠Force. Thus it is not necessary to attack the Nightdome itself because it is possible to destroy it by killing enough of Oliver's shadow summons.

Related Quests

  • ⁠Lift the Shadow Curse

Related items

  • Oliver's Diary

Companion approval

  • Confronting Oliver regarding his identity as Thaniel (I know who you really are, and where you really belong.):  +1
  • Agreeing to play with Oliver  +1  -1  +1  +1  +1
    • After agreeing to play with Oliver, change your mind  +1  -1
  • Agreeing to play a second round with Oliver  +1  -1  +1  +1  +1
    • Finding Oliver without alerting the shadows  +1  +1
    • Finding Oliver after fighting the shadows  -1  -1  +1

Bugs

  • If Oliver's Nightdome is destroyed directly instead of through his summons, Oliver remains hostile and the subsequent dialogue where he returns to Thaniel does not trigger. This seems to render ⁠Lift the Shadow Curse impossible to complete. A possible fix is using  Dominate Person after breaking the Nightdome if Oliver remains hostile and on turn order.
  • If the party members are physically unable to initiate dialogue with Oliver (e.g., from being behind a strategically-placed barricade), Oliver remains hostile until someone leaves the barricade and becomes able to initiate dialogue. Once dialogue is initiated, the fight does not end until all remaining summons are destroyed.
